q: Name one phenomenon in which light behaves like a wave, and one in which it behaves like a particle.
a: Like a wave: the fringe pattern of the double-slit experiment, that is, interference (also diffraction). Like a particle: the photoelectric effect, the Compton effect or the single hits of weak light on a screen.

q: Which photon has the greater momentum: that of red light ($700\,\text{nm}$) or that of blue light ($450\,\text{nm}$)? Justify your answer.
a: That of blue light. The momentum of a photon is $p = \tfrac{h}{\lambda}$, so a shorter wavelength gives a greater momentum: the momentum of the blue photon is $700 : 450 \approx 1.6$ times as large.
